## Finding from Rebase Attempt

I tried rebasing PR #15250 onto current dev but ran into extensive conflicts that need manual resolution:

### Conflicts Found (18 files):
- **Core backend**: `session.ts`, `index.ts` - API changes for archive/unarchive
- **i18n**: 14 language files - new keys added in different order

### Key Conflict Example (session.ts):
\`\`\`typescript
// Dev (HEAD):
if (updates.time?.archived !== undefined) {
  await Session.setArchived({ sessionID, time: updates.time.archived })
}

// Their version handles unarchive (archived: null):
if (updates.time !== undefined && "archived" in updates.time) {
  session = await Session.setArchived({ sessionID, time: updates.time.archived ?? undefined })
}
\`\`\`

### Recommendation:
This PR needs a careful manual rebase by a maintainer or contributor with time for the 18-file merge. The test failures in CI (transform.test.ts lines 1819, 1871) are PRE-EXISTING issues unrelated to this PR - they're failing because new providers were added to dev after this PR was made.

### Test Failure Investigation:
- Expected providers: subset
- Got extra: alibaba, copilot, openaiCompatible, openrouter
- These are NEW providers added to dev after PR creation
- NOT caused by archive feature changes

> I hit this on Windows while trying to install/load `oh-my-openagent` as an OpenCode plugin.
> 
> Observed behavior:
> 
> * OpenCode had a plugin entry configured, but the plugin was not actually installed into the normal runtime path.
> * `opencode plugin oh-my-openagent@latest -g --force` failed with:
>   `request to https://registry.npmjs.org/oh-my-openagent failed, reason: fetch() proxy.url must be a non-empty string`
> * In my shell, `HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / http_proxy / https_proxy` were all set to `http://127.0.0.1:7890`.
> 
> Impact:
> 
> * OpenCode behaved as if the external plugin had not loaded.
> * For OmO specifically, the UI effectively fell back to builtin behavior and only the stock agents were visible.
> 
> Workaround that fixed it locally:
> 
> 1. Create a local cache package dir:
>    `C:\Users\Admin\.cache\opencode\packages\oh-my-openagent@latest`
> 2. In that directory run:
>    `npm install oh-my-openagent@3.15.3 oh-my-openagent-windows-x64@3.15.3 oh-my-openagent-windows-x64-baseline@3.15.3`
> 3. Point the OpenCode plugin entry directly at the local plugin file instead of the npm spec:
>    `file:///C:/Users/Admin/.cache/opencode/packages/oh-my-openagent@latest/node_modules/oh-my-openagent/dist/index.js`
> 4. Fully restart OpenCode.
> 
> After that:
> 
> * `opencode debug config` resolved the plugin and its agents correctly
> * `opencode run --agent 'Sisyphus (Ultraworker)' ...` worked
> 
> So from this machine at least, the regression is consistent with a broken npm/plugin-install path under proxy handling, and using a direct local `file:///.../dist/index.js` plugin entry is an effective workaround.

## Workaround Verified: `--log-level WARN` Effectively Solves Log Bloat

After experiencing the same issue (50GB+ log accumulation within hours with ~100 skills installed), I verified that using `--log-level WARN` completely eliminates the permission ruleset log bloat.

### Verification Results

| Metric | Before (INFO) | After (WARN) |
|--------|---------------|--------------|
| Permission log entries | 900+ per session | 0 |
| Log file size | 16-365 MB per session | 47 KB per session |
| Total log directory | 648 MB | 212 KB |

### Workaround Implementation

Created a wrapper script that always starts OpenCode with `--log-level WARN`:

```bash
# ~/.local/bin/opencode-wrapper
#!/bin/bash
exec /home/USER/.opencode/bin/opencode --log-level WARN "$@"
```

Then added alias in shell config:
```bash
alias opencode="~/.local/bin/opencode-wrapper"
```

### Key Observation

The `--log-level` CLI flag **does work** for the main process. The permission service logs (`service=permission`) at INFO level are suppressed when using WARN level.

This suggests:
1. The P0 fix (move ruleset to DEBUG/TRACE level) would be simpler than expected - just change the log level for permission service entries
2. Users can mitigate immediately with this workaround without waiting for upstream fix

### Suggested P0 Fix

Since the permission ruleset is logged at INFO level, changing the permission service logging to DEBUG or TRACE would solve this completely:

```typescript
// Before (current behavior)
log.info({ permission, pattern, ruleset: fullRuleset }, "evaluate")

// After (proposed fix)
log.debug({ permission, pattern, matchedRule }, "evaluate")  // Only matched rule, at DEBUG level
```

This would:
- Eliminate 148KB per permission log line → ~100 bytes
- Reduce INFO-level noise significantly
- Allow users who need debugging to use `--log-level DEBUG` to see full ruleset

---

**Environment**: OpenCode 1.4.3, Linux, oh-my-openagent plugin, ~100 skills

Even after I stopped `normalizeMessages` from dropping the empty text, I still had empty assistant text getting removed later in the AI SDK request path when `providerOptions` wasn't set. In the broken sessions I was looking at, that was enough to shift the later reasoning blocks and Anthropic rejected the history.

I opened #21860 with a repro for that path too, in case it's useful.

We can reproduce this locally and the behavior matches this issue very closely.

Environment:
- `opencode` version: `1.4.3`
- Anthropic auth plugin: `@ex-machina/opencode-anthropic-auth@1.5.1`
- OS: Linux
- Auth method: `Claude Pro/Max` OAuth

What we verified:
1. `claude` CLI works fine on the same machine:
   ```bash
   claude -p "Respond with OK only"
   ```
   returns:
   ```text
   OK
   ```
2. OpenCode has a valid Anthropic OAuth credential:
   ```bash
   opencode providers list
   ```
   shows `Anthropic oauth`.
3. We re-did the Anthropic login flow from OpenCode (`Claude Pro/Max`) and tested again.
4. The minimal OpenCode request still fails:
   ```bash
   opencode run --print-logs --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 "Respond with OK only"
   ```
   with:
   ```text
   You're out of extra usage. Add more at claude.ai/settings/usage and keep going.
   ```

Important detail: this is happening on a minimal prompt, not a genuinely long-context request. So this looks closer to prompt / identity / billing-path detection than to the separate long-context error classification issue.

Another suspicious detail from the OpenCode log: the failed request still shows the full OpenCode-flavored system prompt under `system[]`, including references like `github.com/anomalyco/opencode` / OpenCode docs text. If Anthropic is keying off prompt-level markers, that would explain why Claude CLI works while OpenCode does not on the same account.

So from our side, we can rule out:
- missing Anthropic credential
- stale login alone
- old plugin version alone
- Claude Max subscription being generally broken

Happy to provide the exact `--print-logs` output if useful, but the short version is: same machine, same account, Claude CLI succeeds, OpenCode fails with `extra usage` on a minimal request.

I traced this to a specific regression:

- introduced in `c9326fc199` (`refactor: replace BunProc with Npm module using @npmcli/arborist`)
- before: plugin resolution used `BunProc.install(...)`
- after: it switched to `Npm.add(...)`

The breaking part is that `packages/opencode/src/npm/index.ts` now constructs `new Arborist({...})` without loading/passing npm config, so Arborist falls back to its default registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org`).

I think the correct fix is slightly stronger than just passing a single `registry` string:

- load npm config via `@npmcli/config`
- pass the flattened config (`config.flat`) into every `Arborist` constructor
- use the same resolved config in `outdated()` instead of the hardcoded npmjs URL

That should preserve scoped registries, auth, and normal npm config layering instead of only fixing the default registry case.

```sh

# set your proxy
npm install oh-my-openagent@latest
```
Then replaced the plugin entry in OpenCode config from an npm spec (`oh-my-openagent@latest`) to a local filesystem path:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"
  "plugin": [
    "~/.config/opencode/node_modules/oh-my-openagent"
  ]
}

Seriously, how hard is it to do the same thing that Gemini CLI has with pressing TAB for interacting with the shell command.

> Is this how cursor does it ? A friend of mine had cursor just open a terminal on his linux pc and he could just write and interact with, then close it with Ctrl+C and the agent did pick it back up at the end of the session. This looks really useful, rather than having the shell inside some sort of opencode "box" imo.

It is a feature that Gemini CLI has, too. 
Which I think is a goated feature because I can press tab and the "CTRL+C" will kill the child shell command but not the actual Gemini CLI. Because sometimes the LLM runs a command that will wait for input or spawns a server that I need to kill or a script that is brute forcing a challenge that is going to take ages to actually solve, etc.
Complete pass through to the shell child running the LLM's command would be amazing for me.

For now, I tell the LLM to use TMUX to run commands in. That way I can connect to the TMUX session from a separate terminal and do what I need to do.
